name: galaxy-mcp: a real tool run lands as a loom-job block and the poller follows it
description: The submission-capture-* scenarios replay recorded galaxy-mcp results through the capture hook; this one sends real submissions. Capture keys on the pi tool name (mcp__galaxy__run_tool) and reads the job ids out of the result as pi's MCP delivers it, so a change in either shows up here as a run that went through with nothing recorded. The agent stages a small BED file by URL, runs Line/Word/Character count (wc_gnu) on it and waits for the result, which keeps the session alive across poller ticks: the scenario asserts the run_tool registration, the loom-job block in notebook.md, and a poll.transition row for the wc_gnu job reaching a terminal state. The history is loom-eval- prefixed for --galaxy-cleanup.
inputs: Create a new Galaxy history named exactly `loom-eval-job-{{RUN_ID}}`. Upload this BED file into it by URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/galaxyproject/galaxy/release_24.0/test-data/1.bed . Then run the Galaxy tool `wc_gnu` (Line/Word/Character count) on that dataset with default settings. Wait until the wc_gnu job has finished -- check on it every so often -- and then tell me how many lines the BED file has according to the tool's output. Skip the formal plan; this is a quick check.
